As for what he says—"show me any one man who could remain alive from St. Paul's age to the day of judgment"—it is spoken in the ordinary manner of speaking by way of <term>amplification</term> <note>original: "amplification"—a rhetorical device used to emphasize a point by expanding upon it or using an extreme example.</note>, and as it were at the largest extent. It is to be understood as referring to someone who should be born a little after that age. And should he not be born within a short time after, whose forerunners were causing such a <term>coil</term> <note>original: "coile"—meaning a great stir, disturbance, or fuss.</note> while the Apostles were living? The Book of Revelation, speaking of the Antichrist under that seventh Head, says: *And another is not yet come, Chapter 17:10.* We are accustomed to use this kind of phrasing in matters that are so near that they may seem to have arrived, even though they have not come yet; and we do not speak this way at all regarding things that are to come fifteen hundred years later.

All the things, therefore, which you would infer from this are idle and trifling, as if you would prove by Beza’s reason that Peter and Paul were Antichrists, and that Simon Magus and Nero were, as it were, Christs. Why do you not (I pray you) try to prove that the origin of the Antichrist was not even close at hand at that time? Is it not enough for the confuting of his "singular person" <note>A "singular person" refers to the Catholic argument that the Antichrist is one specific individual human being rather than an office or institution.</note> if he should have his beginning some ages after Paul? But you, like an unskilled <term>fighter at sharp</term> <note>original: "vnſkilfull fighter at ſharpe"—a fencer or duelist using unblunted, lethal swords rather than practice foils.</note>, hold up your shield to keep off a blow where none is offered to you; and where you are actually struck and wounded even to the death, you never care how naked and ill-guarded you leave yourself.

The second argument of Theodore Beza is this: that individual kings and kingdoms are not understood by the singular names of these beasts—the Bear, the Lion, and the Leopard—in Daniel, Chapter 7. One of these contains many kings within it. Therefore, Paul in the same manner understands one body (as it were, made of many tyrants) and not one single person by the "man of sin" and the "son of perdition," since Paul agrees with Daniel.

This is the summary of it: *Antichrist has not yet come, because he did not arrive at the times when certain people from both the past and more recent times thought he would.* The ancient figures you speak of are the **Thessalonians**, **Cyprian**, **Jerome**, **Gregory**, one **Jude**, **Lactantius**, and the **Bishop of Florence**. The more recent figures are the **Samosatenians** of Hungary and Transylvania, **Illyricus**, **Chytræus**, **Luther**, **Bullinger**, and **Musculus**. In pursuing this matter, you spend the entire chapter.

I answer in two ways. First, it is false to claim that because he did not arrive at the times mentioned by those authors, he has not yet come. It was not necessary for them to know the exact origin and rising of Antichrist. The "Beast" remains a mystery long after he has been revealed (Revelation 17:7). His person was manifest, but his wickedness and true origin were not. For the mystery would be taken away if what lay lurking within were revealed to everyone. 

And just as the Kingdom of God—though it was foretold by the Prophets—did not come with observable signs <note>original: "observation," referring to Luke 17:20, though the text cites Luc. 17:25</note>, neither did the kingdom of Antichrist. Weeds are sown while the farmers sleep (Matthew 13:25). They are not noticed when they first sprout; yet, are they not there at all simply because the farmers did not notice the stages of their growth? Should we deny that the sun is shining just because we cannot see it moving forward? 

Without a doubt, that most crafty enemy of mankind [the Devil] would prefer his Vicar <note>The author likely refers to the Pope as the "Vicar" or earthly representative of the Devil/Antichrist.</note> to resemble his own nature: to creep in quietly so that he might surprise more people before they notice him, rather than rushing in with a shout and an uproar that warns men to look out for their own safety. 

Furthermore, when you conclude that he is not yet come, you should have considered all the other possible times leading up to the present, and not only those few dates mentioned by the ancient and modern men you cited. Can a person be said not to have arrived on an appointed day just because he didn't show up at the first or second [hour...]

You answer *that the ancient Fathers were deceived by an opinion they held about the end of the world, which they believed to be closer than it actually was; and therefore, they held this false opinion about Antichrist being closer than he was in truth.* To this I say: if the ancient writers had based their opinion about Antichrist’s approach solely on their belief about the end of the world, it would be necessary that as they erred about the latter, they would also have erred about Antichrist. 

But seeing as they grounded their opinion upon other arguments, and seeing that they concluded not so much that Antichrist drew near because the end of the world was at hand, but rather that the end of the world approached because Antichrist was at hand, that which they affirmed regarding this matter must be firm and stable—unless you can show us that the rest of their reasons are as flimsy as their opinion was mistaken regarding the end of the world. 

It is evident by their words that they suspected the end of the world to be at hand because of Antichrist's coming, and not the other way around. For Jerome reasons *that Antichrist was at hand because "that which hindered" was taken away.* Gregory gathered *just as much from the fulfillment of all things that were foretold;* and what more certain argument can there be than that? And you yourself confess *that all the ancient writers, considering the wickedness of their times, suspected that the time of Antichrist was hanging over*

<header>CONCERNING ANTICHRIST. Chapter 3.</header>

Therefore, they did not conclude that Antichrist was coming simply because they suspected the world was ending. For the ultimate end is never treated as a sign of the things that precede it; rather, the things that come before are treated as signs of the ultimate end, since the end is the final event and the most unknown of all things—even to the angels themselves and even to the Son of Man (Matthew 24; Mark 13:32, 36). The end cannot provide forewarning of events that occur before it and are better known than it is. Therefore, they knew by certain arguments that Antichrist was soon to come, but their additions regarding the ultimate end relied only on the uncertain conjectures of men. They had received a false chronology from Clement of Alexandria (*Stromata*, Book 1) claiming that 5,784 years, two months, and twelve days had passed from Adam to the death of the Emperor Commodus.

To this was added the opinion that the world would last for six thousand years. Because of this, Cyprian says in the preface to his *Exhortation to the Martyrs*: *"Six thousand years are now almost complete since the time that the Devil began to fight against mankind."* The statement from Lactantius in the 7th book of his *Divine Institutes*, Chapter 25, also came from that idea: *"All the time we look for in this world is no more than the space of two hundred years."* If we add to these their conjecture that the world would expire quickly and immediately after Antichrist’s arrival, then it will easily appear that there is a great difference between their teachings on Antichrist and their statements about the end of the world. The former <note>The arrival of Antichrist.</note> was certainly made known to them by many prophecies and undoubted signs; the latter <note>The timing of the world's end.</note> was something they were persuaded of by its apparent likelihood and by the weak authority of men. 

We see a similar situation with Christ's disciples, whom we know expected a physical, earthly kingdom <term>original: "temporal Kingdome"</term>. Yet, when they preached that Christ had come and that the kingdom was then to be restored to Israel, should anyone—failing to see that kingdom restored—deny credit to their report of Christ’s coming? If someone did deny it, would they not be acting unfairly? For the disciples knew that Christ had come through the most certain and infallible arguments; however, their ideas about a physical kingdom were drawn from the dregs <note>original: "drugs"</note> of common error.

In the same way, the ancient writers understood by true signs from the Scriptures that Antichrist was at the very doors. Therefore, you have not escaped with this answer of yours, for the judgment of the ancient fathers remains ratified and immovable: that Antichrist has come. 

It was not without reason that one of your own side, the Bishop of Florence <note>likely referring to Bishop Ranieri of Florence, who in 1105 was accused of preaching that Antichrist was already born</note>, openly declared five hundred years ago *that Antichrist had come at that time*. The Council of Florence was called and gathered to suppress him, but you have thought it safer for yourselves that the fame of this council should reach posterity rather than the actual records of its proceedings.

Regarding later writers, you first mention the *Samosatenians of Hungary* <note>original: "Samofatenians"; a sect following the non-Trinitarian teachings of Paul of Samosata</note>, with whom I will have nothing to do. I do not care what they think or do not think until they are of a sounder mind than they are now. 

The rest of the learned men differ in three ways in their judgments regarding the time of Antichrist's coming: *Illyricus, Chytraeus*, and *Luther* place the coming of Antichrist around the year of our Lord 600. *Bullinger* places it at the year 763. *Musculus* at the year 1200. 

The reason for their judgment was this: because they were such quick-scented <term>keen-scented or perceptive</term> men, the second uprising of the Beast—the timeframe in which they were focused—smelled so strong to them that they could not bring their minds to think of any time before this. In this, they are like good hunting dogs who, once they have smelled the place where the wild beast hides, are carried away with a full cry and run after it with all their might, no longer sniffing out every single one of its footsteps. 

Therefore, for the most part, they attribute things to the second arising of the Beast which actually belong to the first; they apply many things to it that do not fit. However, this slight error regarding the time of his uprising does not mean he has not come at all. Rather, we may know that Antichrist has come by the shouts and outcries they make, even if they were ignorant of the exact moment when he first began to exist <note>original: "subsist"</note>. 

Let us, therefore, review your answers to each of them, so that you may understand—not so much that they were in error, but that you have exhausted yourself to no purpose in laboring to overthrow their opinions.

### Against the first demonstration that *Antichrist* is not yet come, taken from the *universal preaching of the Gospel*.

**T**his question about the time of *Antichrist’s* coming gives the greatest light to the truth of all the rest, being as it were the sun that enlightens all the other stars with its light. It is framed thus; I pray you allow me to put it into form so that those of us who are of the more unrefined and simple sort might more easily notice this art of yours in making demonstrations.

> He who is to come after the preaching of the Gospel in the whole world has not yet come. But Antichrist is to come after the preaching of the Gospel in the whole world; therefore, he has not yet come.

This is your manner of demonstrating, in which we encounter many marvelous and newfound matters that were never delivered by any of the masters who profess the art of demonstration—namely, that such principles should be used in demonstrating which are neither true nor primary. For as for their truth: the proposition is either manifestly false or at least doubtful, as it shall appear more clearly later, and therefore it is not fit for use in a demonstration.

Besides, if a man should doubt the assumption, what strength can it have from that passage in Matthew? What single word is there in his Gospel concerning Antichrist’s coming after a universal preaching? How is this an "immediate principle" which, if it has any credibility at all, must borrow it from another place? Pardon me, I pray, if I am somewhat more meticulous and harder to please than you may think necessary. I thought it necessary to make a trial of one of your demonstrations; since we have now gotten a taste of what "sweet" ones they are in this first and foremost of its fellows, we shall not need to be so precise in examining and scanning the rest. We may judge the whole pack of them by the specific quality <note>original: "qualicum"</note> of this first "proper" fellow.

But even you yourself saw how it was not worth a rotten nut <note>original: "deafe nut" — a hollow or decayed nut</note>, much less worthy of the name of a demonstration. <header>CHAPTER 4. AGAINST BELLARMINE,</header>

In the meantime, I affirm that you do not only dispute unskillfully, but dishonestly also, and like a Jesuit. For there being a threefold division of time—past, present, and to come—nothing can be proved to be in the future unless it is first established that it is neither present nor past. While you, therefore, conclude that Antichrist is to come after the general preaching of the Gospel because he cannot exist together with it? But why, I pray you, may he not come before it? Indeed, what if he must necessarily come before, by the very force of this demonstration of yours?

Certainly, he cannot exist together with the general preaching because of the cruelty of the persecution (for those are your own words), and he cannot come after it, for Christ says: *that when once the Gospel should be preached in all the world, then shall the end come.* <note>original: "consummation"; referring to Matthew 24:14</note> You see that nothing comes between the universal preaching and the end of all things. Therefore, by this "excellent" reasoning of yours, it must follow that he should come before the universal preaching. This is not the least virtue of this doughty, "undoubted" demonstration: that it does more to help your adversary’s cause than your own. 

But you say that your adversaries do not accept this reasoning. Truly, I believe your friends do not either, unless they are some little crafty foxes who would say that the ugly, out-of-tune crow is a pretty nightingale, or a nightingale’s companion for its sweet singing. But I give you thanks at last <note>original: "I cunne you thankes"</note> for acknowledging the absurdity of this demonstration, after becoming exhausted and weary from fussing <note>original: "puddering"</note> about it. Besides, you say: *that you have no leisure now to make this demonstration strong and unanswerable by laying open its undeniable principles, and therefore that you will prove the same point out of the testimonies of the Church Fathers.*

What a kind of speech is this that has dropped from you? Do you have no leisure to make demonstrations and to prove them sound—you who have set upon such a grand piece of work, a truly unparalleled work <note>original: "None-such"</note>, the most comprehensive handling of all controversies, which might serve as a "Treasury of Controversies"? Especially since you bring no single argument of any weight to this cause? I cannot help but notice here a crafty Jesuit’s simple tactic <note>original: "shift"</note>. That which you cannot do because of the poverty and badness of your cause, you make us believe you have "no leisure" to do, because of the haste you make toward other matters.

For whereas you say that Paul speaks of a matter already past in *Romans 10:18*, you might have remembered from Augustine that he used the past tense for that which was yet to come, just as David had done (whose words they are, as you yourself wrote a little earlier). The Prophets are accustomed to speaking almost everywhere of things to come as if they were already past. In the other Scriptures, Paul speaks of that matter as already perfected <note>original: "perfited"; completed or fulfilled</note>, which the Lord foretold was to be perfected.

## Chapter 5.

### *Against Bellarmine's second demonstration taken from the desolation of the Roman Empire.*

The second demonstration is taken (as you say) from another sign that goes before the time of *Antichrist*, which shall be a total desolation of the *Roman Empire*; which, seeing it endures to this day, *Antichrist* has not yet come. Upon this, you undertake to prove two things: both that *Antichrist* will not come until after the Empire of *Rome* is altogether laid waste; and then that the Empire of *Rome* endures to this day. You confirm the first point out of four scriptures. Among these, the first three—namely *Daniel 2* and *7*, and *Revelation 17*—rely upon the interpretation of *Irenaeus, Book 5.* <note>Irenaeus (c. 130–202 AD) was an early Church Father whose work "Against Heresies" influenced many later interpretations of prophecy.</note>

But I pray you, let us set aside the authority of men, and let us weigh the matter itself in the balance of truth. If the matter were to be examined by the opinions of men—which are often contrary to one another, and of which many might be brought forward regarding these most dark and obscure passages—we would never make an end. Let us work it out instead from those principles by which we may be led to something that is certain.

Therefore, regarding the second chapter of *Daniel* and that succession of the chief kingdoms which were to be on earth until the end of the world—which the *Image* shows—it points out the four principal kingdoms that should be on earth by the head of **Gold**, the breast of **Silver**, the belly of **brass**, the legs of **iron**, and the feet partly of **iron** and partly of **clay**. These are: the *Assyrians*, the *Persians*, the *Greeks*, and the *Romans*. Of these, that of the *Romans*, which is the last, was (as you say) divided into two parts for a very long time, just as the legs are two and the longest of all the parts. Besides that, ten toes sprouted up out of those two legs, and the whole *Image* ended in them, because the *Roman Empire* was to be divided eventually into ten *Kings*—because there shall then be no single *King* of the *Romans*, just as a toe is not a leg. Regarding these things, I ask: what single word is there in this entire vision by which the coming of *Antichrist* may be suggested?

# CONCERNING ANTICHRIST. chapter 5.

The Roman Empire is one entity in a sense, but its manner of government by diverse magistrates and types of rule is varied. It could not be said that "five Roman Empires have fallen," but rather "five kings," who were rulers and governors of that one Empire. <note>The author is interpreting the "seven heads" of the Beast in Revelation as seven successive forms of Roman government.</note> Besides, Antichrist is that seventh Roman king; for the Angel says so expressly: *And the Beast, which was, and is not, is both that eighth king, and one of the seven* (verse 11).

There was no such desolation; rather, the prostitute of Rome <note>original: "whore of Rome"—a common Reformation-era term for the Roman Catholic Church based on the "Whore of Babylon" in Revelation 17.</note> flourished exceedingly, as she was carried on the back of this king-like Beast. Therefore, the Roman Empire was not to be destroyed when Antichrist was to come; instead, it was to be marvelously preserved, increased, and expanded during the time appointed by God. Let us therefore understand that Paul and John speak of the same hindrance, but the Angel describes it more expressly and clearly by its location, its dignity, and its number. By these plain and true signs, we should be led, as if by the hand, to the very cradle and infancy of the Antichrist.

Luther, Illyricus <note>original: "Luther Illyricus"; referring to Matthias Flacius Illyricus (1520–1575), a Lutheran reformer and historian who wrote extensively on church history.</note>, and Chytraeus <note>original: "Chytreus"; David Chytraeus (1530–1600), a prominent German Lutheran theologian.</note> conclude on solid grounds that by the restoring of the Empire through the Pope's help, he is that great Antichrist.

# AGAINST BELLARMINE. Chapter 6.

You prove that the Book of Revelation speaks specifically of Enoch and Elijah because it says *that they shall be slain by Antichrist, and that their bodies shall remain unburied three days in the street of the great City, and that they shall rise again after three days and ascend into heaven; which things, as you say, never happened to any man until this day.* I answer that I have already made it plain, based on the chronological order and the consistency of all the facts, that all these things have been accomplished already—specifically when the Fathers of the Council of Trent <note>The Council of Trent (1545–1563) was a major Roman Catholic ecumenical council held in response to the Protestant Reformation.</note> cut the throats, as it were, of the Holy Scriptures by robbing them of all their authority and binding the interpretation of them to the Pope's cursed chair. Moreover, what John says regarding the death of these Prophets provides us with a necessary argument against your literal interpretation of those two specific individuals.

For Enoch <note>original: "Henoch"</note> died in no other way than by that translation <term>In biblical theology, "translation" refers to being taken directly into heaven by God without experiencing physical death.</term> of his long ago, as the Apostle says: *“By faith Enoch was translated so that he should not see death, and he was not found, because God had translated him; for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God”* (Hebrews 11:5). The state of Elijah is much the same. For God is always consistent with Himself, and He always gives the same rewards to similar people for similar ends. Therefore, they are not to be slain by Antichrist. 

But you will object that Tertullian <note>An early Christian author and theologian (c. 155 – c. 220 AD) from Carthage.</note> says in his book *On the Soul* <note>original: "De Anima"</note>, Chapter 28: *“That Enoch and Elijah were translated, and their death was not found—that is, it was deferred—but they are reserved to die so that they may destroy Antichrist with their blood.”* I answer: Tertullian offers nothing but a mere conjecture that these figures whom Revelation speaks of are Enoch and Elijah. Since the Apostle teaches plainly and clearly that Enoch *was translated so that he should not see death,* we may now easily choose which of these two to believe. It does not become holy men to assert and vow their own blind opinions against the manifest words of the Scriptures.

[Antichrist] in the last hour, is not yet come; Antichrist must come in the last hour; therefore, he is not yet come. I bring your reasoning into a formal structure <term>original: "into forme"; referring to a logical syllogism</term> so that you may see and be ashamed of your usual manner of arguing. The syllogism <term>Syllogism: a form of logical reasoning where a conclusion is drawn from two given or assumed premises.</term> has one more "foot" than it should <note>Likely referring to the logical fallacy of the "four-term syllogism," where an ambiguous term creates an invalid argument.</note>. Otherwise, if your proposition includes all the time from the first coming [of Christ] to the second, it is completely false. In your second assumption, you take the "last hour" as John <note>The Apostle John, specifically referring to 1 John 2:18: "Little children, it is the last hour..."</note> uses it, meaning the whole era of grace until Christ comes a second time. Or, if it is taken more strictly to mean three and a half years, it is a senseless begging of the question <note>original: "begging of the thing in question"; a logical fallacy where the conclusion is assumed in the premise.</note>, and John's authority is cited to no purpose. 

You provide a simile to illustrate John's argument, and you want him to speak of Antichrist in the same way someone might speak of the sun. When the sun is rising, a man might call its beams "the sun"; you say his argument is strong in that same way, as if a man were to argue concerning the last hour of the night: 

*The sun rises in the last hour of the night; the beams of the sun now make the air bright; therefore, this is the last hour of the night.* 

I answer that this comparison is fitting enough to express what the Apostle [John] means. For the beams of the sun and the sun itself are always seen during the same hour. Therefore, he who defines this entire last age as only one "hour" did nothing wrong by placing its forerunners at the beginning of it. 

But as for you, who define the "last hour" as only three and a half years, what help can you get from this comparison of the sun and its beams? How unlike the sun he is, and how unlike the sun's beams his ministers are! The beams precede the sun for scarcely half an hour, and then the sun rises immediately and offers itself to be seen for twelve hours. Since you feel yourself pressed by this man's <note>Irenaeus, an early church father who suggested the name Lateinos</note> authority, seeing it as a heavy prejudice against your cause, you thought it fit to first weaken his authority. ### Chapter 10: AGAINST BELLARMINE

It is taught that the long *i* <note>original: *j*; in Early Modern English, 'i' and 'j' were often interchangeable, and 'j' was used to represent the long 'i' sound</note> among the Romans was usually pronounced like the diphthong *ei*, and that it had a slender *e* included within it. For example, Cicero wrote *Bini* <note>meaning "two each"</note> in Latin to represent the Greek *bine* <note>original: βινεί (*binei*), a Greek verb; Cicero discusses this in *Familiar Letters* 9.22 regarding how innocent Latin words could sound like Greek obscenities</note> in the ninth book of his *Familiar Letters* to Papirius Paetus; the beginning of that letter is: *"I love your modesty."* <note>original Latin: *Amo verecundiam tuam*</note> Even today, we both pronounce and write *celeberrimi* (most famous), *vis* (power), *Primus* (first), and *captivi* (captives)—words which are also found in ancient inscriptions written as *Celeberrimei*, *Veis*, *Preimus*, and *Captiuei*. Therefore, although we write *Latinos* today, we must not doubt that in ancient times it was written with a diphthong, just as Irenaeus undoubtedly used it. Similarly, the ancient Greeks expressed the "great Hiriq" <note>original: *Hirick*; a Hebrew vowel representing a long 'i' sound</note> of the Hebrews indifferently, sometimes with a simple *i* and sometimes with *ei*. This is why, in Christ’s cry of complaint, *"Eli, Eli..."* <note>Matthew 27:46; "My God, my God"</note>, the words are written by some as *Mei* or *Imei*, as the scholar Johannes Drusius has observed. Therefore, the objection you raise regarding the spelling is trivial and of no importance at all.

Would such a challenger not be cursed with "bell, book, and candle" <note>a reference to the formal ceremony of excommunication</note> for daring to usurp what properly belongs to the Roman See? Far from this name not being proper to any Pope, it is proper to all of them during the time they hold the Chair, seeing as the Antichrist is a succession of Bishops and not a single individual, as we have clearly proven before. Fourthly, you say that Gregory Nazianzen <note>original: "Gregory Nazianzene." But because we have added the numerical name *Latins* <note>original: "Latinos"</note> to the previous Marks, lest perhaps you should object to the same thing here that you did with those, I would have you know in a few words regarding it that this name is most ancient. Who does not know this? And yet, this name lay neglected <note>original: "throwne vnder the bench"</note> for many ages until the Emperors moved their seat to Constantinople. Then it began to gain some little life again and to be in demand, as is clear from Epiphanius <note>Epiphanius of Salamis (c. 310–403 AD), a prominent bishop and theologian known for his writings against heresy.</note>, who, speaking of the Romans in his book *On Weights and Measures*, says that they were not yet called Romans but Latins.

But this name was not yet so frequently used, nor so forced upon the Churches, that it had the status of a "Mark." This is why Socrates, Theodoret, Sozomen, and Evagrius <note>A group of 4th to 6th-century ecclesiastical historians.</note> use the term very sparingly; whenever they speak of Rome, they call it "the elder Rome," and they distinguish the provinces using only the names of the East and the West. However, after the second Beast began to act arrogantly <note>original: "keepe a ruffling"</note> and turned all things upside down, and a partition of the Empire was made and boundaries were set by Nicephorus, the Emperor of Constantinople, and Charlemagne <note>original: "Charles the Great"</note>, then the name of the "Roman Provinces" continued only in the Western countries. The Eastern provinces were called by the common name of the "Latin Provinces," as can be seen in the works of the historians Zonaras, Nicetas, Gregoras, and Chalcocondyla <note>Influential Byzantine historians writing between the 12th and 15th centuries.</note>. 

Afterward, it was not enough for the Greeks to subject themselves to the Roman Patriarch (for they claimed the title of "Roman Patriarchs" for themselves); rather, superiority had to be given to the "Latin Pope," or to the Bishop of ancient Rome, or else no reconciliation could be made. This is apparent from the Council of Lyons under Gregory X <note>The Second Council of Lyon (1274), which attempted to reunite the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic churches.</note>. Therefore, although these and many other superstitions were in use many years before Antichrist was made known to the world, once they were used as bonds to tie men to defend the errors of the Church of Rome, they took on the nature of brands, marks, and stamps <note>original: "Characters"</note>. But if that glorious Antichrist, whom you [Bellarmine] invent and devise, should come in between, how could this bounty of God be shown upon those who lay before in such miserable affliction? The second place of scripture for this purpose is taken out of that excellent song of Moses, Deuteronomy 32:36, etc.: *“When the Lord shall judge his people, then shall he repent because of his servants, when he shall see that their strength is gone, and that neither he that is shut up, nor he that is let go can do them any good; when he shall say, ‘Where are their gods? And the strong rocks to whom they committed themselves for defense?’”* Moses sings of these same times in that place, and he shows that the Jews are to be brought into an extreme and desperate misery when God shall arise to avenge the cause <note>original: "reuenge the quarrell." In this context, "quarrel" refers to a legal cause or a ground for complaint that requires vindication.</note> of his people. The third place is out of those words in Isaiah 49:14: *“But if Zion says, ‘The Lord has forsaken me,’ etc.”* To these may be added Jeremiah 30:8, etc.; Ezekiel 37; Daniel 12; and Hosea 3:4–5. These few places may suffice to open the meaning of many others. From these I conclude that although the Pope of Rome shall never be a Jew, nor be received by the Jews as their Messiah, but instead be hated by them, yet this is no barrier to keep him from being the great and Grand Antichrist. Indeed, unless these things were so, he would differ from the primary and most significant Antichrist, as we have declared in the appropriate places.

### Concerning the Seat of Antichrist.

In explaining the words of this prophecy, we have concluded with very strong arguments that Rome is the Seat of Antichrist, and that this began immediately after the Empire was taken away from the pagan <note>original: "heathen"</note> Emperors. But where these heads remain fixed, there must the Antichrist’s seat necessarily be. Moreover, since we have proved before by many arguments that Antichrist was already existing as soon as Constantine entered upon his kingdoms, he has had no other seat but at Rome. Though the Pope stayed at Avignon <note>original: "Auenion"; referring to the "Babylonian Captivity" of the Papacy (1309–1376) when the popes resided in France.</note> for a few years, he did so only as a temporary visitor, with no intention of permanently changing his seat.

The *argument* stands as follows:

I answer that this proposition is false, and that it relies entirely upon a distorted <note>original: "peruerse"</note> understanding of the unity of the Church. For the "Church" is both *commonly* and *properly* so called.

Are there as many Temples of Jerusalem as there are individual faithful men? Paul speaks to the Corinthians with words that apply to every Christian: *Do you not know that you are the Temple of God? And if any man defile the Temple of God...* (1 Corinthians 3:16–17). *Know you not that your body is the Temple of the Holy Ghost?* (1 Corinthians 6:19). I will not even mention those places which I cited just now. 

You are a more skillful <note>original: "deliver"</note> and agile fellow at being a master builder than Solomon was, for you can build up so many Temples in so short a space of time. # Chapter 13. AGAINST BELLARMINE,

I answer that the ancient Fathers, both Greek and Latin, have spoken just as the Scriptures speak. As **Clement of Alexandria** <note>original: "Clem. Alexandr: stromat. book. 7."</note> says in Book 7 of the *Stromata*: *A Temple is either a great one, such as a Church—which is an assembly of faithful people—or else a little one, such as an individual person who retains the seed of Abraham.* And as **Cyprian** speaks in Book 1 of *Against the Jews*, Chapter 15: *That Christ should be the house and Temple of God, and that the old Temple has ceased, and the new one has begun.* And in Book 5, Epistle 8: *Although charity should not drive us so much to yield help to our brethren, yet we ought to consider in this place that these people who have been captured are the temples of God; and we ought not to allow the temples of God to remain long in captivity through our delay in helping them and our neglect of their grief.* 

But you say that you do not mean either the Christian assemblies or individual faithful people, but rather the houses and material churches where we meet together to worship God publicly. I answer that you therefore dispute like a "profound scholar" <note>original: "profound Clercke"</note> who, despite all this, does not actually prove your point with this grand answer. For you now argue this way: 

1. No material churches built for public worship were called "Temples" among the Christians for many centuries. 
2. But "Temples" are the places appointed for public worship. 
3. Therefore, there was no kind of "Temple" among the Christians for many centuries. 

What of that, I ask you? For even if there was not *that* specific kind of material temple, there was still another kind of Temple among the Christians even in those very same centuries you speak of—and it is in such a Temple that the Antichrist would sit afterward. 

Unless, perhaps, you suppose that the holy place of assembly is the *only* thing that qualifies as a Temple. If that were so, the Antichrist would be Antichrist no longer than the time he actually sits inside those physical churches. Or else, if he can be Antichrist while outside of those churches, then the Great Antichrist can exist outside the "Temple of God." And though he might not boast of himself as if he were God, he would still be Antichrist. However, this sacrilegious boasting of himself happens only while he sits in the Temple of God, as is clear from the Apostle's words. Thus, we would have a new "Captain Antichrist," the likes of whom the Apostles never saw through the spirit of prophecy.

There is great force, I suppose <note>original: "I wis"</note>, in your arguments, which bring forth such monsters of logic as this everywhere. But let us go further with you. Now, where you say that the name of a "Temple" *was not given to houses of prayer until Jerome's time, whom you cite for it,* I would have you...

Having previously cited earlier Fathers, the author now provides evidence from Eusebius and other historical sources to show that material Christian churches were indeed called "Temples" long before Bellarmine admits, and further argues that the "Temple" where Antichrist sits refers to the Christian assembly or the human conscience rather than the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem.</meta>

-> TOUCHING ANTICHRIST. chap. 13. 739 <-

Understand that Eusebius, who was more ancient than Jerome, did not refrain from calling them by this name. In *Ecclesiastical History*, Book 10, Chapter 2, Ruffinus <note>Rufinus of Aquileia, a monk and historian who translated Eusebius from Greek to Latin</note> describes it this way in Book 9, Chapter 10: *The places newly revived rise up more gorgeously and loftily built, and high and stately Temples are reared up instead of those former humble and poor meeting houses.* <note>original: "base and poore Conuenticles"</note> And again, Eusebius says in Book 10, Chapter 13: *A Temple was built in Tyre after a bountiful and stately fashion by his care and endeavor, which was the most notable Church in all the country of Phoenicia.* 

So also in that laudatory oration <note>a speech of praise</note> which one made regarding the building of the Churches that were dedicated to Paulinus, the Bishop of the Tyrians, we read these words: *And you who are the majestic ornament that sets out the holy Temple of God that has been newly built here.* And after many other words in the same place, we read: *He built up this most magnificent Temple of the most high God.* 

Indeed, the Holy Spirit, wisely providing a way to counter your crafty schemes, <note>original: "Crafty conueiances"</note> so guided the hands and pens of those who wrote about that time—when Antichrist should first appear and emerge <note>original: "peere & peepe out"</note>—that they should give the name of a "Temple" even to the holy places of the Christian assemblies. This was done so that it might be made evident in every way that he sits in the Temple of God. 

Therefore, you conclude this matter by saying it seems certain that the Apostle Paul spoke of the Temple of Jerusalem because, in writing that Antichrist should sit in the Temple of God, he said something he wanted to be understood by those to whom he wrote—and they could not then understand any other Temple but that of Jerusalem. However, you may easily see how false this is (to say nothing worse of it, though I could and still speak truly).

The Thessalonians might understand that he should sit in the minds and consciences of men whom he would seduce with his craft and hypocrisy, as **Anselm** <note>Anselm of Canterbury (c. 1033–1109), an influential medieval theologian</note> interprets it. Or they might understand that he should reign in the Christian assemblies, as **Chrysostom**, **Theodoret**, **Theophylact**, and **Oecumenius** <note>These are all prominent Greek Fathers and biblical commentators</note> explain it. Or they might understand that he would brag about himself as if he were the Temple and the Church, as **Augustine** explains it. 

But as for the Temple of Jerusalem, they could never once think that he meant that. They knew it would be completely destroyed, according to what Christ foretold of it in *Matthew 23:39* and *24:2*. They also knew it would never be built again, seeing that the wrath of God seized upon the Jews to the very last, as it says in *1 Thessalonians 2:16*.

To these you add the "common interpretation" <note>original: "exposition"</note> of the Church Fathers, as you say. However, the contrary opinion of those cited above will not allow it to be considered common; the ignorance of a few ought not to stand in the way of such a clear truth. These are your arguments, the force of which I now leave the reader to judge. I will briefly see <note>original: "see in a word"</note> what I can say to your answers, in which you try to weaken the arguments of some of our writers.

First, whereas our men object based on Revelation 17—*that Rome is the chief seat of Antichrist, because this seat is a great city which sits on seven hills and which has a kingdom over the kings of the earth; all of which things are found to be in Rome*—you answer in three ways. 

First, you claim *that "Rome" is not meant by this city, but rather the whole kingdom of the Devil.* But you do not rely on this answer, nor is it in truth of any importance <note>original: "moment"</note>, since the universal kingdom of the Devil is not what shall be burned up by the ten kings—especially since many wicked men will remain alive to bewail its fall (Revelation 18:9). For how shall the whole company perish if some citizens remain afterward? 

Casting this answer aside <note>original: "behind the doors"</note>, you move to another: you grant that Rome is understood by "the Whore," *but argue it is heathenish Rome—the Rome that reigned then, worshiped idols, and persecuted Christians—and not Christian Rome.* 

I answer that you do poorly to separate those things which the Holy Spirit has joined together. For Rome is the Whore and the seat of Antichrist precisely when she is carried by the Beast; but she was not "carried" while the heathens reigned. For she is carried by the seventh head, which had not yet come when John received this prophecy (Revelation 17:9–10). 

Besides, if the "Whore" is the heathenish Rome that then reigned, then Antichrist must have come during the time of that heathenish Empire. ## Chapter XIV.

### *Of Antichrist's Doctrine.*

We teach and hold—and that from the Scriptures themselves, as the Holy Spirit has also taught us from them—that the doctrine of Antichrist is full of hypocrisy, fraud, and crafty subtleties. It is designed so that it may deceive even those who are otherwise the most prudent men, if the Holy Spirit does not go before them with the light and lantern of His holy truth. For we have need of singular prudence to know this Beast thoroughly, as one who has "two horns like the Lamb" <note>A reference to Revelation 13:11, describing a beast that appears Christ-like but speaks like a dragon.</note> and who is the false prophet that seduces the world. 

On the contrary, the Pope’s advocates <note>original: "proctours"</note> insist that this same doctrine of Antichrist is so openly impious and blasphemous that no man could be so dull <note>original: "blockish"</note> that he would not perceive and detest it upon first hearing it. To make this point plain, O **Bellarmine**, you reduce all this doctrine of his to four heads: 

1. First, that he shall deny Jesus to be Christ, and therefore he shall labor to overthrow all the ordinances of our Savior, such as Baptism and Confirmation; and he shall teach that circumcision, the Jewish Sabbath, and other ceremonies of the Old Law have not yet ceased. 
2. Second, he shall affirm that he is the true Christ who was promised in the Law and the Prophets. 
3. Third, he shall affirm that he is a God and will have himself worshipped as a God. 
4. Lastly, he shall say that he is the only God, and he shall stand against all other gods—that is, both the true God as well as false gods and idols. 

And from this, you take four arguments to claim that the Pope is not Antichrist: because he does not deny Jesus to be Christ; neither does he bring in circumcision or the Jewish Sabbath; neither does he make himself to be Christ, nor yet to be a God, and least of all to be the only God; and moreover, he worships images and departed saints. What force these arguments have to prove what you intend, we shall see afterward by

And what did Boniface VIII <note>Pope from 1294 to 1303, known for his extreme claims of papal authority over temporal rulers.</note> declare when he said: *We declare, define, and pronounce that it is absolutely necessary for salvation to be subject to the Roman Pontiff.* (From the *Extravagantes* <note>original: "Extrauag."; a collection of canon laws that "wandered" outside the main decrees.</note> on superiority and obedience, in the decree *Unam Sanctam* <note>original: "Unam Sanctam"; a famous papal bull issued in 1302 asserting that there is no salvation outside the Church and that the Pope holds supreme power.</note>).

But you say he does not acknowledge himself to be God because *he acknowledges himself to be God's servant.* I am ashamed of your arguments! It is as if blessing and cursing, horrible blasphemy against God, and counterfeit obedience to God could not come from the same cursed mouth. You know he calls himself the "servant of servants" <note>original: "servus servorum Dei"; a traditional humble title used by Popes, which the author views here as hypocritical.</note> when it suits his words, and yet, whenever he pleases, he acts as the "king of kings."

The fourth point is that *he shall exalt himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped* (2 Thessalonians 2:4). Regarding this, you claim he will not allow any God—neither true nor false—nor any idols. You have already received an answer to this argument earlier when we discussed the common name of Antichrist. There, we showed that the Apostle does not mean a heavenly God, but an earthly one—that is, civil magistrates <note>In the Early Modern period, rulers and judges were often referred to as "gods" in a civil sense, based on Psalm 82:6.</note>, who are worthy of respect and are to be honored outwardly. 

This is also how the passage in Daniel should be understood: *And he will not respect the God of his fathers, nor will he care for any god, because he shall rise up against all.* (Chapter 11:37). Jerome <note>St. Jerome (c. 347–420 AD), the scholar and Church Father who translated the Bible into the Latin Vulgate.</note> interprets this sacrilegious pride as a kind of excessive power over all religion. For he says: *And Antichrist shall wage war against the saints and shall overcome them; and he shall be exalted with such great pride that he shall endeavor to change the laws of God and the ceremonies, subjecting all religion to his own power.* (*Commentary*).

## Chapter XV.

### Of the Miracles of Antichrist.

Regarding the miracles of Antichrist, *there are, as you say, three things set down in Scripture: First, that he should perform many miracles; secondly, that they should be lying miracles; thirdly, that there are three examples of miracles specifically mentioned.* In all these things I easily agree with you. But why do you not show us, through all of this, that the Pope neither works many miracles, nor lying miracles, nor any of those three miracles that are mentioned by name? If you did, you might make it plain that the Pope is in no way related to the Antichrist. 

By this omission, you seem to have been afraid of a fair trial. But whether you fear it or not, whether you want to or not, you and your Pope must be brought to your great **Inquest** <note>original: "Inquest"; a legal inquiry or judicial investigation</note> regarding this point. Without any doubt, you neither can deny—nor do you have any desire to deny—that your Pope and the Antichrist resemble one another as notably as two twins in the working of multitudes of miracles. Indeed, this is one of the principal marks by which your Church boasts that she is known to be the only true Catholic Church. 

Therefore, there is no controversy about the first point. But let us examine the next point for a moment. Let us see whether those miracles which have been performed by the Popes and their **journeymen** <note>original: "iourny men"; subordinates or agents who perform work for a master</note> since the time that the Antichrist first began to show his head are "lying wonders" or not. In this way, it may also appear whether our men are slandering you with the truth. 

I will not use that argument which the Holy Spirit makes to be a most certain discovery of false miracles—namely, that whatever serves to nourish and establish error and superstition is to be accounted as a fraudulent and false sign. (For you will not acknowledge your errors, even though this argument is enough to persuade those who are...)

Regarding the leprosy, it may appear from this to be a most filthy forgery, because the ancient writers—who either flourished immediately after Constantine or else lived at the same time as him—did not mention it, not even in a single word. Eusebius, who wrote Constantine's life so diligently and gathered whatever he could find from any source to commend him—after the manner of those who give declamatory orations in praise of great princes and states—would surely never have buried in silence such a singular blessing of God bestowed upon him. 

The later writers, therefore, must have dragged all this out of some sinkhole at third hand, namely out of the Romish "tale-books" <note>likely referring to legendary hagiographies such as the *Golden Legend*</note> which were compiled for this purpose alone: to amplify the Pope's authority among blind people who are ready to swallow such morsels greedily. Besides, since the healing of this leprosy depends upon his baptism, and since it is most certain that he was baptized at Nicomedia by Eusebius, the Bishop of that place, and not at Rome by Sylvester—and that not at the beginning of his reign, but in the last act of his life—who does not see that this healing of his leprosy is altogether faked and forged from the brains of brain-sick and lying authors? 

Eusebius reports *that he was baptized at Nicomedia a little before he departed from this life* (in *The Life of Constantine*, book 4). And to him we may join as witnesses: Socrates (book 1, chapter 39), Theodoret (book 1, chapter 32), Sozomen (book 2, chapter 34), Ambrose (in *The Death of Theodosius*), and Jerome in his *Chronicles*.

Is it likely that these latecomers should know the truth more certainly, when they were farther away from any means of finding it out? But let us see in a word what grounds each of them relies on.

Regarding the baptism of Constantine, and knowing as well what the ancient men had delivered concerning this matter—in order to make both their accounts "hold water"—one reporter <note>This likely refers to a later chronicler trying to reconcile conflicting accounts</note> records in his Chronicles that *he was baptized at Rome, but he was rebaptized by Eusebius of Nicomedia, the Arian Bishop.* But he did not give diligent heed to what ancient history records, which says with one consent *that he deferred his baptism until toward the end of his life, because he desired to be baptized in the Jordan.* How could he have deferred it if he had already received it before at Rome? 

Besides, this chronicler deals rashly and unjustly with the godly Emperor by charging him with so grievous a crime as revolting from his faith. Constantine was so constant in his belief that neither Eusebius of Nicomedia nor any other of the Arians <note>Arianism was a theological movement that denied the full divinity of Christ, declared heretical at the Council of Nicaea</note> could ever withdraw him from the truth. Indeed, while he lived, he used his authority to keep them all down, so that they neither could nor dared to do anything against the faith that was established in the Council of Nicaea (Socrates, Book 2, Chapter 2). 

Furthermore, the Council at Ariminum <note>modern-day Rimini; the council was held in 359 AD</note>, writing to Constantine’s son <note>Constantius II</note>, abundantly testifies in that letter that he persevered constantly in the true faith to the very end of his days. They said: 

> *“We have judged it to be an absurd thing, now that Constantine the Great has departed from this world, having been baptized into the true faith, and has therefore gone to his rightful resting place of joy in heaven, to go about making any new articles of faith here, and thereby show contempt toward so many holy confessors and martyrs.”* 

These words do not describe a man who had fallen from the truth. And again after that, they said: 

> *“We do, moreover, beseech you to grant us this: that nothing may be either taken away from those things which have been ordered and decreed of old, nor yet anything added, but that all those things may remain entire and inviolable which have been preserved to this very day through the piety of your father.”* (Theodoret, Book 2.12; Sozomen, Book 4.18). 

God forbid that we should think he made any shipwreck of his faith and requested a second baptism from an Arian.

But Eusebius, who is a witness who was living at the time, tells us that immediately upon seeing that miraculous apparition in the heavens, Constantine called the Christians to him. He was taught the whole way of salvation by them, he gave his mind to reading the Holy Scriptures, he honored the priests greatly, and he promised that he would worship no other God afterward (Eusebius, *The Life of Constantine*, Book 1). And he was as good as his word, as is evident from those proclamations he made in favor of the Christians, which he caused to be published when he reigned together with Licinius (Eusebius, Book 10, Chapter 5). 

Was he not already a Christian before Sylvester initiated him? After all, he waged war against Licinius on this very dispute: because Licinius treated the Christians so poorly and with so little courtesy. As for the report *that Peter and Paul appeared to him in a dream by night and commanded him to send for Sylvester, and that he asked Sylvester whether there were such gods worshiped among the Christians as those called Peter and Paul*—these things are exceedingly ridiculous and incredible. What witnesses, I ask you, could say that Peter and Paul appeared to him by night? To whom did Constantine tell this? Did he tell it to Sylvester and not to Eusebius? 

How could he be ignorant of the God of the Christians, having been taught long before and so perfectly by Christians, and having read the Scriptures himself, and having vowed that he would have no other God but Christ (as we just showed from Eusebius)? It is a marvel that he did not send for Sylvester until he was told to do so by a vision, given that he was so familiarly acquainted with the holy ministers from the beginning of his conversion that he made them his companions. All wise men will agree when those of the Church of Rome prove themselves to not be playing tricks <note>original: "legerdemaine"</note> in this and in most other matters, like a company of cheating <term>cogging mates: deceptive or dishonest companions</term>. But Constantine had received from God a faith just as precious as that of the rest of the saints, and therefore he might be a partaker of the Spirit, just like those men on whom the Spirit fell before baptism (Acts 10:44, etc.). Now, as for the fact that he deferred <note>delayed</note> his baptism, the Church Fathers knew that he did not delay it out of contempt, but through a certain religious intent that he had (I will not now dispute whether it was good or bad). They might also think that Moses did not consider his children to be strangers from the covenant even though they were not circumcised on the appointed day, and that the Israelites were not forbidden to offer sacrifices, nor were they kept from the rest of the worship of the Tabernacle, though they were not circumcised in the desert. 

Therefore, there was no cause why they should deny him entrance into the Council, seeing as every delay of the outward sign does not take away from the faithful the privilege of being the sons of God in the common duties of piety, either before God or men. Seeing, therefore, it is certain that Constantine was not baptized until the end of his life, that report touching the cleansing of Constantine's leprosy by Sylvester through the power of baptism—which was supposedly administered at least twenty years before—is a lying fable. And this is something that Jacobus de Voragine <note>a 13th-century chronicler and author of the *Golden Legend*</note> ingenuously acknowledges in his legend of the invention <note>discovery</note> of the Holy Cross; speaking of the baptism of Constantine: *"It is doubted,"* (he says) *"whether he deferred his baptism, whereupon there is doubt made likewise about that legend of St. Sylvester, in regard to many things therein;"* and a little further on, *"It is certain that there are many things in the history..."*

The second miracle concerns a bull raised from the dead by Sylvester. The story goes that Zambres—the last of those twelve Jews who attacked and argued against the Christian truth—put the bull to death suddenly by whispering certain words into its ear. This fable is of the same quality as the previous one. There are none of the ancient writers—whether they were living at that time or followed immediately after—who speak even a single word regarding this matter. The reason was plain: the author who was the creator <note>original: "moulter"</note> of this worthless invention <note>original: "droffye deuise"; drossy refers to the scum or impurities on melting metal.</note> had not yet been born; he eventually based it on the debate between Justin Martyr and Trypho the Jew. 

To this we may add that Zonaras <note>Joannes Zonaras, a 12th-century Byzantine chronicler.</note> records the matter as if Helena, Constantine’s mother, was residing in Rome together with her son. However, the legend claims she was absent in Judea during her son's conversion, and being offended <note>original: "stomacking the matter"</note> by the fact that he had become a Christian, she went in great haste from there to Rome with 149 of the most learned Jews, so that she might test what the truth was through a formal debate. Furthermore, the legend is not only inconsistent with Zonaras, but even with itself. For it says in the *Life of Sylvester* that Helena went to Judea before her conversion; but the *Golden Legend* <note>A famous medieval collection of hagiographies by Jacobus de Voragine.</note> (in the story of the "Discovery of the Cross") says that she went after her conversion, for it claims she went to seek the Cross of the Lord. And it is certain that she never took this journey more than once; it is also certain that she was an old woman before she went, and that she departed after her grandchildren were made Caesars, as Eusebius reports in the *Life of Constantine*, Book 3. This miracle also relies on no other grounds than such unreliable witnesses as these; whether it is a lying wonder or not, I now leave to the judgment of the reader.

### CHAPTER 15. AGAINST BELLARMINE

...recited this miracle; it would be a foolish task to go about refuting such foolery. By these miracles of Sylvester's <note>Pope Sylvester I (reigned 314–335 AD), around whom many medieval legends were invented.</note>, therefore, we may judge the rest. But perhaps you will say that these things are reported falsely of him. I answer that it is all the same, whether the Pope himself performs false miracles, or whether false ones are attributed to and associated with him by his followers and supporters. All his miracles tend toward one end: that the Beast <note>A reference to the Beast in the Book of Revelation, whom Protestant reformers commonly identified as the Papacy.</note> may be adored—that is, that the Pope may be honored with the highest honor possible.

Secondly, I say that miracles had ceased by the times of Chrysostom and Augustine; for so says Chrysostom in his 6th Homily on the first Epistle to the Corinthians, Chapter 2. He gives a reason why miracles were performed in the time of the disciples and yet there are none in his time: *because the more certain and necessary matters are, the less our faith needs them. A little further on, he says that the more certainly an argument is demonstrated, the more it takes away from the reward of faith, and therefore signs were not performed at that present time.* So also says Saint Augustine in his book *Of True Religion* <note>original: "De vera religione"</note>, Chapter 25: *For since the Catholic Church is scattered abroad throughout all the world and founded in it, those miracles were not permitted to endure until our times, lest our minds should always seek after visible things, and mankind should grow cold in religion through seeing them performed routinely—at the strangeness of which religion originally grew hot. Neither ought we now to doubt, but rather we must believe those men who, when they speak of such things as few men attain to, are nonetheless able to persuade the multitudes of people that they are to be followed.*

But again, they say, "Why are the miracles not performed now which are said to have been performed then?" I could say truly that they were necessary before the world believed, so that the world *might* believe. Whoever now inquires after miracles to make him believe makes himself worthy of being wondered at for his monstrous unbelief; he will not believe when all the world believes. These testimonies prove all Popish miracles (which are almost infinite) to be full of fraud and cozenage <term>cozenage: deception, cheating, or trickery</term>, at least since that time. And certainly, God seems to have put an end to those old miracles before that age in His singular providence, so that Antichrist and his copesmates <term>copesmates: companions or associates, often used here to imply partners in crime</term> might be better identified by the world, when he should be seen to come forth with this strange and pompous display of miraculous feats.

Thirdly, there are not wanting some of your own company who have...

But this is no strange matter with Jesuits, who are openly reported (and that by the confession of many of the "unclean birds of your own feather" <note>Meaning other Catholics or former Jesuits who have exposed their secrets.</note>) to make no conscience at all of cheating and dissembling, lying, and faking in everything they take in hand, so long as it serves their own and their master's advantage. Indeed, it is no marvel that Xavier performed that host of admirable exploits among the Indians which Maffei, Ribadeneira, and Torsellini <note>original: "Mapheus Ribademeirus and Turfellinus" — Giovanni Pietro Maffei, Pedro de Ribadeneira, and Orazio Torsellini were prominent Jesuit biographers who wrote hagiographies of Xavier and Ignatius.</note> talk about so much, seeing he was far enough away to avoid having his claims examined and discovered while he was among them in such remote places. Do you give any credit to those Indian writings? You may remember, if you will, that late design of the Jesuits in publishing a book to this effect: to spread a rumor among the people and persuade them that Theodore Beza <note>Theodore Beza (1519–1605) was a major French Protestant Reformer and the successor to John Calvin in Geneva.</note>—that arch-enemy of the Pope and all Popery—was dead and buried. They claimed that before his last gasp, he was converted to your Roman religion by the efforts of one of his own side, and that many other citizens of Geneva, being moved by his example, renounced their former errors and embraced Popish doctrine with all their hearts. It cannot slip out of your memory...

For first, we have declared that these things are to be interpreted figuratively, not literally. These miracles are common not to any one single man, but to a specific kingdom, such as we have proved this great *Antichrist* to be; now, such things as are common to a kingdom cannot apply to many individual persons except figuratively. Besides, if these miracles were personal and specific to one individual, then how could they come to the knowledge of the whole world so that it would follow the *Beast* with such great admiration, as the *Revelation* describes? Those things which are only heard of do not move and work upon men’s minds as much as those which are seen with the eyes. CONCERNING THE REVELATION. Chap. 18.

<image-desc>A horizontal decorative band consisting of repeating ornamental fleurons separates the header from the chapter title.</image-desc>

## The 18th Chapter of the Revelation.

### The Logical Analysis <note>original: "logicall Resoluing"; a systematic breakdown or outline of the chapter's arguments and structure</note>.

*Up to this point, we have heard in what manner and style the Throne of the Beast <note>original: "Beast"; in Protestant theology of this era, the Beast was typically identified as the Papacy</note> is formed. The description of this was the first and a lighter sprinkling of the fifth Vial <note>original: "Viall"; the Vials (or bowls) in Revelation represent divine judgments poured out upon the earth</note>. Now follows a more plentiful pouring out of it, which is joined with the ruin of this Throne itself. We distinguish this into those things which come before its ruin and those things which follow after. These things are accomplished by the ministry of three angels, two of whom declare this destruction in plain words. The first is a glorious angel (Verse 1), who declares it more concisely (Verses 2–3). The second Minister, who is unnamed, declares it more fully: first, by exhorting the godly to flee out of Babylon (Verses 4–5), and also by inciting those who were to be the instruments of this destruction to use due and deserved severity (Verses 6–7). Then, he describes the destruction, partly by the bitter lamentations of the wicked kings (Verses 9–10), of the wicked merchants (Verses 11–16), and of the wicked oarsmen <note>original: "oare men"</note> and sailors (Verses 17–19); and partly by the joy of the godly (Verse 20). So much for the ministry of the two angels. The third angel uses a sign in addition to his words, which is both proposed (Verse 21) and explained—summarily in that same verse, and specifically in Verses 22–24. So far, these are the things that precede this ruin. That which follows it is a thanksgiving, which the saints offer to God for it (Chapter 19, Verses 1–4).*

# THE EXPOSITION.

**Verse 1.** *And after these things I saw an Angel descending.* Here we see how God will make His admirable patience manifest to all the world when He goes about the destruction of the City of Rome. For besides all the former warnings that He had given it—which were so many, and of so many kinds, both fair and foul—He does not come down to execute His last judgment against it until He first sends three Angels, by whose voices men might be admonished to avoid the plague that was rushing in upon them. 

The first of these is *an Angel coming down from heaven*. This is some excellent and worthy man, such a one as should come suddenly, before he is expected, as those things do which slip down from heaven. Those things which spring up among us on earth yield some show and sign of themselves before they grow to their ripeness; but those that come from heaven can be upon us, and in the midst of us in a moment, so that we can perceive no foresight or foreknowledge of them beforehand. 

So in the 10th Chapter, *an Angel came down from heaven* when many stout patrons of the truth arose on a sudden, of whom there was no suspicion before. And this selfsame thing is confirmed by other places which may be gathered from this interpretation. This Angel seems to be one who shall be suddenly converted to the Truth, who shall thereby make it manifest to all men that he comes down from heaven. Such was that "descending" in the tenth Chapter, where men who had been nuzzled <note>original: "nousled"; meaning nurtured, brought up, or entrenched, often in the sense of being fed or fostered in a particular belief</note> long in superstition were made the nurslings of the truth and true piety on a sudden. 

This *Angel has great power*. But to what end? Since there is no worthy exploit of his spoken of, it may be that this is he to whose charge the demolishing of this Throne <note>referring to the Papal throne or the seat of power in Rome/Babylon</note> is committed. He shall not so much bring a new prophecy touching the ruin of Babylon as he shall show himself ready to put that matter into execution—which the Oracles of God had often foretold would happen.

Thirdly, *the earth was made bright with his glory*, because even those who are strangers to the true Church shall honor and admire him...

### OF THE REVELATION. Chapter 18.

For the luster of his piety and the notable majesty that shall shine forth in him, he shall have a good report and testimony from those who are outside, as the Apostle says in 1 Timothy 3:7. The similar meaning of these words, which we have seen used in the previous chapters, helps us to know what kind of Angel this will be, even though he is yet to come. And this is the only way to dive into the depth of these mysteries, which otherwise are unsearchable to us. But we must observe that this Angel shall not come forth (as it seems) immediately after that manifestation of the Throne which we spoke of in the previous chapter. Rather, he shall come at length after some certain and convenient time passes in between; and therefore this vision is divided from the former by that usual way of expressing a passage of time—one that is a little further disjointed from what went before—namely, "and after these things I saw."

**Verse 2. And he cried out mightily.** The words are "in" or "with might"—that is, strongly, valiantly, and vehemently. The *Complutensian Polyglot* <note>original: "complut"; referring to the Complutensian Polyglot Bible, the first multi-language edition of the entire Bible, printed in Spain</note> and the King's Bible <note>likely referring to the King James Version or a similar authorized royal edition</note> read "with a strong voice"; Aretas <note>Aretas of Caesarea, a 10th-century Greek commentator on the Book of Revelation</note> also reads it this way, but the meaning is exactly the same. This vehement lifting up of the voice signifies the effectiveness and the unchangeableness of the matters that were to be acted out, as Aretas notes. And yet, perhaps such a denouncing of them is not to be expected through literal words; rather, the very onset of the event shall stir up such an impression <note>original: "immaginaciō"</note> in the minds of men that it will be as if they were hearing this voice sounding in their ears.

He cries with a redoubled voice that "Babylon is fallen, is fallen," following the manner of the former prophecies, but with this difference: those earlier ones announced a ruin that was to come long after, while this one teaches that it is at hand—even now in sight—and at last to be accomplished upon his arrival. That "great Babylon"—that is, Rome, the seven-hilled city and sovereign empress, just as Babylon was the mother city of the Assyrians long ago. There is a double Babylon spoken of in this book, as we learned in Chapter 16; that is, Rome...

*And it has become the habitation of devils.* The cause of its ruin is not mentioned here in these specific words, as that follows later in verse 3. Rather, its desolation is declared by comparing it to a horrible and hideous wilderness. This is notably expressed by the kind of inhabitants mentioned here, who gladly stay in solitary and vast places—or rather, it is not so much that they delight in them, as they are sent and thrust down there against their wills. Whereupon, what is first called a "habitation of devils" is immediately after called a "cage of every unclean spirit." That is, it is a prison or house of correction into which they are crowded at the pleasure of their Highest Judge. It is as if these unclean spirits were tormented by God’s most just judgment in these very places after being deprived of all companionship with mortal men—whom they previously abused like slaves by enticing them into sin and wickedness. 

To be thus driven from the company of men is like Hell to them, seeing as they consider it a kind of comfort to ease the bitter torments of their damnation by drawing men into the same torments with themselves. Yet they are not so shut up within these secret and solitary places that they do not sometimes wander <note>original: "vagary it"</note> and wreak havoc among the greatest crowds of people whenever it seems good to God to permit them. Nevertheless, such wild and waste places are the ordinary prisons appointed for them. The words of Christ seem to refer to this: *When the unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he walks through dry places, seeking rest, but finds none* (Matthew 12:43). 

Moreover, the evils that have been brought into the churches by hermits and monks prove abundantly how greatly the delusions of Satan prevail in those forlorn and desert places, as the most learned Theodore Beza <note>a prominent 16th-century Protestant reformer and scholar</note> has observed. We learn from this passage how the words of Isaiah <note>original: "Esay"</note> 13:20–22 and again Chapter 34:13–15 are to be understood. # OF THE REVELATION. Chapter 18.

The words used here are appropriate—namely, "devils" and "unclean spirits." This is how the Greek interpreters translated that passage, partly retaining the Hebrew words *Tfiiim* <note>original: "Tfiiim"—referring to wild desert creatures</note> and *OThim* <note>original: "OThim"—referring to howling spirits or jackals</note>, and partly turning the Hebrew word *Sehirim* into *Daimonia* <note>original: "Dajmoria"—meaning demons</note>. This is the sense in which the word is used in Leviticus 17:7: *And they shall no longer offer their sacrifices to demons* (literally, *Le-Sehirim*). The word properly means "goats," but it is applied to devils, who often appeared to those who served them as hairy beings, covered in thick, rough hair like water spaniels or Irish rugs <note>original: "Iriſh Rugges"—a type of coarse, shaggy woolen fabric from Ireland, used here to describe a hairy appearance</note>. They are commonly called Satyrs, and Aquila, the Greek interpreter, translates the word in Isaiah as *Trichion* <note>original: "Toikionos"—meaning hairy creatures</note>.

**And a place wherein to keep every unclean bird.** It is not called this because it is like a cage or a coop from which the unclean birds cannot fly out, but because they are seen to keep and have their place of residence most commonly and usually in these ruined places. These are flesh-devouring, ravenous, and unlucky birds, such as the eagle, the kite, the hawk, the vulture, the crow, the night-wandering screech owl, the owlets, and so on. Many of these kinds are listed in Leviticus 11:13. These kinds of birds were counted as unclean by the old Law of Moses. This distinction no longer applies today, and yet they are still aptly called "unclean" because they notably lay before our eyes the nature of filthy and ravenous men who live by stealing and extortion. Such men know no other way to sustain themselves except through violence and wrongdoing toward others. For this reason, this kind of predatory bird is hated by all the other birds—as shown by the way birds flock together to harass one of these "harpies" whenever they find it alone. Likewise, these kinds of ravenous oppressors are hateful and detestable among all mortal men.

**Verse 3. *For all nations have drunk of the wine.*** Here the Holy Spirit comes to the causes of Babylon's ruin, which are said to be three: that she was the ringleader of idolatry to all men; that she enticed the kings of the earth to partake in her wickedness; and that she enriched and promoted all her citizens beyond measure with her excessive luxury and rioting. These sins of hers were committed long ago, and many ages before this they were often laid to her charge by other angels. The fact that she is still accused of the same crimes shows the wainscot forehead <term>wainscot forehead</term> <note>A "wainscot forehead" is a metaphor for being thick-skinned, brazen, or shameless, like a wooden panel.</note> of this whore—for she remains hardened in her ways.
